note: Japan's visa exemption arrangements for short-term stay, as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' table gives them (74 countries and regions, last changed 1 September 2025 with Montenegro): 90 days for the European Union's members and most others (Austria, Germany, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Mexico, Switzerland and the United Kingdom may extend to six months at the Ministry of Justice, not modelled), 30 days for Brunei and Qatar, 15 for Indonesia and Thailand; Qatar's and Indonesia's passports must first be registered for the waiver (taken as an ETA). Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports, and Taiwan's with an identification number, are on the list; some entries ask a machine-readable or biometric passport. Every other passport needs a visa. MOFA, the Immigration Services Agency and Japan's embassies all refuse this client (403), so the table is read from Wikipedia's copy of it, citing MOFA, and agrees with the reported changes (Montenegro on 1 September 2025, Brunei's 30 days from 10 December 2024). JESTA, the planned travel authorisation, isn't in force.

sources.title: Japan National Tourism Organization, Visa information
sources.said: Passport holders of some countries (and some regions) do not need a visa if their period of stay in Japan is 90 days or less and they are only engaging in tourism activities. Please refer to the List of Countries and Regions that have Visa Exemption Arrangements with Japan: https://www.mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/short/novisa.html
